---
title: "Read a special mean curve"
description: "Find natural parameters for constant, decentred, affine and first-harmonic mean curves."
---

The special-case functions return coefficients on the scale used to
describe the mean curve. For a constant mean, the natural parameter
`mu` is a direction in radians.

```{r}
library(CircularRegression)
data(bison)

d <- na.omit(bison[seq_len(180), "y.dir", drop = FALSE])
fit <- meanDirectionModel(d, response = "y.dir")
fit$natural_parameters
```

| Mean curve | Function |
|:--|:--|
| Constant direction | `meanDirectionModel()` |
| Decentred curve with an angular predictor | `decentredPredictorModel()` |
| Affine vector with a continuous predictor | `presnellModel()` |
| First-harmonic vector with an angular predictor | `jammalamadakaModel()` |

For the affine and first-harmonic forms, use `natural_orientation` when
reconstructing the two vector components. `natural_stability` records
whether the ratio parameterization is numerically stable. The standard
errors shown in the example use independent observation contributions,
which matters when interpreting results from a single movement track.

[Examples of all four curves](angular-regression-workflow.html#special-case-wrappers).
